name: Microsoft SQL Server
tagline: Microsoft's flagship RDBMS: T-SQL, columnstore, Always On, and now native vectors and JSON.
description: SQL Server is the default relational database of the Microsoft world, running on Windows and Linux and sharing its engine with Azure SQL. It is a strong all-rounder: row and columnstore indexes in one database, In-Memory OLTP, temporal tables, Always On availability groups and very good tooling (SSMS, Query Store). SQL Server 2025 (GA November 2025) added a native vector type with DiskANN indexing, a native JSON type, regex functions and change event streaming. It is the obvious choice for .NET and Windows-heavy shops; the costs are per-core licensing, the fact that its best features sit in Enterprise Edition, and no built-in way to scale writes horizontally.

pricing.notes: Per-core (Standard/Enterprise) or Server+CAL licensing, or pay-as-you-go via Azure Arc. Free Express and Developer editions.

scale.notes: Scales up well; readable secondaries and distributed availability groups for reads/DR. Write scale-out requires app-level sharding.

strengths: Columnstore and rowstore indexes on the same tables give real HTAP without ETL
Query Store, Intelligent Query Processing and SSMS make performance work approachable
Always On availability groups provide automatic failover with readable secondaries
Native vector type and DiskANN index in 2025 put semantic search next to relational data
Same engine as Azure SQL, so lift-and-shift to Microsoft's cloud is straightforward
Deep integration with .NET, Entra ID, Power BI and the wider Microsoft stack
weaknesses: Per-core Enterprise licensing gets expensive quickly on large servers
No native horizontal write scaling or sharding
Linux support lags Windows for some features (e.g., certain HA and integration services)
T-SQL dialect and features tie applications to Microsoft
useCases: ERP and CRM back ends (Dynamics, many ISV products)
Departmental data marts feeding Power BI
Hybrid on-prem and Azure deployments via Azure Arc
notIdealFor: Budget projects that need Enterprise-only features
